summary: Dark Souls franchise entries added as supplemental sourced guide rows; Sami did not list these in the locked personal spine.

entries.title: Dark Souls

primary.why: Dark Souls originally released on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, followed by the Windows Prepare to Die Edition. Dark Souls: Remastered later released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Switch, with higher resolution and 60 fps targets on the modern non-Switch routes. Windows Remastered is the strongest capture/settings route and includes the Artorias of the Abyss content.
primary.how_to_play: Use Dark Souls: Remastered on Windows through Steam. Use the original Prepare to Die Edition only for historical comparison or mod-specific preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use Prepare to Die Edition only for original-version comparison or mod-specific needs; it is not the main archive route.

entries.title: Dark Souls II
entries.definitive_edition: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin on Windows

emulation.notes: Native Windows Scholar of the First Sin.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows Scholar of the First Sin

primary.version: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin
primary.why: Dark Souls II released on PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Windows, then Scholar of the First Sin bundled the base game with the three DLC campaigns and added a higher-fidelity PC/PlayStation 4/Xbox One version. Scholar is the complete Dark Souls II experience, and the newer PC/PS4/Xbox One version also has remastered visuals, 1080p/60 fps, revised enemy placement, and expanded multiplayer support.
primary.how_to_play: Use Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin on Windows. Use the 2014 original only if intentionally comparing the old enemy/item layout.

entries.remaster_caveats: Scholar changes enemy/item placement and balance versus the original release; use the 2014 version only for comparison, not as a separate required content route.

entries.title: Dark Souls III
entries.definitive_edition: Windows version with both DLC expansions

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC with both DLC expansions

primary.version: Dark Souls III with Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City
primary.why: Dark Souls III released on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Windows, with two DLC expansions and The Fire Fades Edition bundling the base game and both expansions on console. Windows with both DLC installed is the highest-fidelity complete route because it has the best capture/settings ceiling and the full expansion content.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows Steam version with Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City installed. Verify online/server state before documenting multiplayer features.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster replacing the Windows route is logged; verify online/server state before multiplayer capture.
